clips.text: Gracie, my apple muffins are under there.
clips.script: [thick New York accent, mild, plaintive] Gracie, my apple muffins are under THERE.

clips.text: Oh, honey. Nobody has to turn off the lights. We'll come back. Every full moon. I'll bring apple muffins.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, tender, melting] Oh, honey. [warm Long Island accent, warm, reassuring] Nobody has to turn off the lights. We'll come back. Every full moon. [warm Long Island accent, brisk, gentle] I'll bring apple muffins.
[sheepish, small] Tah Tah. At the apple muffins.

clips.text: Apple muffins! Deedee brings the teachers APPLE MUFFINS?
clips.script: [astonished, delighted] Apple muffins! [scandalized, shrill] Deedee brings the teachers APPLE MUFFINS?

clips.text: Dad’s in his recliner. Mom has the apple muffins. They’re fine. They’re probably fine.
clips.script: [quiet, steady] Dad’s in his recliner. Mom has the apple muffins. [thin, hopeful] They’re fine. [uncertain, low] They’re probably fine.

clips.text: Long Island is under glass now, you know. Mr. Vance put a dome over it. It’s very safe. Your mother is in her kitchen, making apple muffins.
clips.script: [matter-of-fact] Long Island is under glass now, you know. Mr. Vance put a dome over it. It's very safe. Your mother is in her kitchen, making apple muffins.

clips.text: Besides, you just got here. Go see your mother. She made apple muffins.
clips.script: [warm, friendly] Besides, you just got here. Go see your mother. [relishing, drawn out] She made APPLE MUFFINS.

clips.text: I'll stay here and guard the apple muffins, Deary.
clips.script: [thick New York accent, dignified, relieved] I'll stay here and guard the apple muffins, DEARY.

clips.text: Tom! Sit. Eat. I made apple muffins. Yes, I know it's nine in the morning. Do not argue.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, warm, bustling] Tom! Sit. Eat. [warm Long Island accent, proud, firm] I made apple muffins. Yes, I know it's nine in the morning. [warm Long Island accent, sweet, warning] Do not argue.

clips.text: Your apple muffins are under California, Boppy. Don't move. I'm presenting.
clips.script: [crisp, presenting, unbothered] Your apple muffins are under CALIFORNIA, Boppy. [firm] Don't move. [grand] I'm PRESENTING.

clips.text: Deedee. I’m going to eat the apple muffins now. Okay? Okay.
clips.script: [gentle, resolved] Deedee. I’m going to eat the apple muffins now. [soft, brave] Okay? Okay.

clips.text: She’s looping. Look at the tray. Same apple muffins. Every time. They’re fresh, they’re perfect, and nobody ever eats them.
clips.script: [quiet, sad] She’s looping. Look at the tray. [careful, flat] Same apple muffins. Every time. [aching, soft] They’re fresh, they’re perfect, and nobody ever eats them.

clips.text: Nobody gets hurt. Nobody gets old. Nobody gets left. Your mother’s inside. She’s fine. She’s making apple muffins.
clips.script: [thick New York accent, flat, recited] Nobody gets hurt. Nobody gets old. Nobody gets left. [thick New York accent, gentle, proud] Your mother’s inside. She’s fine. [thick New York accent, flat, mechanical] She’s making apple muffins.

clips.text: A layover! Where? Never mind. Take a sweater. Actually, take two. And take the apple muffins.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, bright, thrilled] A layover! Where? Never mind. [warm Long Island accent, brisk, fussing] Take a sweater. Actually, take two. And take the apple muffins.

clips.text: Inside. She’s fine. She’s making apple muffins. Don’t look at the porch.
clips.script: [thick New York accent, evasive] Inside. She’s fine. She’s making apple muffins. [thick New York accent, hurried] Don’t look at the porch.

clips.text: And the apple muffins are excellent.
clips.script: [thick New York accent, dry] And the apple muffins are excellent.
